scope: Exploratory extension specified after primary EN-TEx results and before any scores for these three assays
selection: Complementary accessibility, active promoter-associated mark and repressive mark; selected from available source assays before fitting; no score-based selection
label: Supplied imbalance_significance per informative heterozygous SNV/experiment; not binding presence, tissue differential activity or causal variant effect
folds_seeds_contexts: Existing 5 chromosome folds x 3 seeds x strict/1hop; all locus repeats stay on their chromosome
encoder_policy: Canonical graph/checkpoints/NT revision frozen; only original logistic probe trained
report: All assays and contexts, including nulls; paired hierarchical fold/seed bootstrap; six exploratory contrasts with fold sign-flip/BH as a sensitivity; no independent biological replicates inferred from seeds
limitations: Static segment features predict per-measurement imbalance; no donor-specific allele direction; graph donor membership remains transductive

prediction_followups.equal_locus_weight: Each test measurement has weight 1 / number of test measurements at its locus within the assay and run; labels remain per measurement
prediction_followups.eligibility: Every fold must meet count thresholds; eligibility based only on labels/counts, shared across seeds, contexts and feature sets
prediction_followups.macro: Equal weight over the same eligible tissues (or donors) within each fold/seed; then paired hierarchical fold/seed bootstrap
prediction_followups.normalized_ap: (AP - weighted positive prevalence) / (1 - weighted positive prevalence)
prediction_followups.limitations: Pointwise exploratory intervals; overlapping training folds and multiple analyses. Donor/tissue stratification is not donor/tissue-held-out fitting. Reweighting changes evaluation, not the original training objective.

followups_definition: Added during this implementation, before any new-assay smoke scores were inspected; thresholds reused unchanged from the completed primary-assay follow-ups
